# Founder Brain

- **Founder:** Priya Raman
- **Business:** Lumen Skin
- **Track:** b2c
- **Hybrid:** false
- **Stage:** Under 10k a month, roughly 4k GBP
- **Locked:** 2026-08-21

## Thesis

I make a three-product range for people whose skin reacts to everything, so they can stop spending money on things that make it worse. I make it because that was my face for two years.

## Offer

Three-product skincare line for people with reactive, easily irritated skin. A cleanser, a barrier cream and a single serum. Deliberately small range.

Direct to consumer through the website. Cleanser 22 GBP, barrier cream 34 GBP, serum 41 GBP. Bundle at 84 GBP, which is where most of the revenue sits. No subscription yet.

The problem in customer language: "Everything I try makes my face worse and I've got a cupboard full of half-used bottles I wasted money on."

Why Priya: developed the formulas after two years of her own eczema and rosacea flare-ups, working with a cosmetic chemist. She is the customer, and the range exists because nothing on the shelf worked for her.

## Audience

**Persona.** Women 28 to 45, mostly UK. Sensitive, reactive or compromised-barrier skin, often with a diagnosis behind it, eczema, rosacea or perioral dermatitis. Has spent hundreds on products that did not work and is sceptical of anything that sounds like marketing.

**What they want.** To stop reacting. Not glow, not anti-ageing. A face that is calm and predictable, and to stop wasting money finding out what sets it off.

**Attention map.** Instagram most of all, saving and sharing rather than commenting. TikTok for skincare research, especially dermatologist accounts and ingredient explainers. Reddit for honest reviews, r/SkincareAddiction and r/Rosacea. Follows dermatologists and ingredient-focused creators rather than lifestyle beauty influencers.

**Adjacent purchases.** Fragrance-free laundry detergent, mineral SPF, gentle cleansing balms, prescription topicals from a GP or derm.

## Proof

- 340 customers, 31% have reordered.
- 47 reviews averaging 4.7. The recurring word in them is "calm".
- Two customers with photo evidence of a six-week change, both consented to use.
- Formulated with a cosmetic chemist. Patch tested. Fragrance free.
- Priya's own story, which is the strongest asset she has and the one she uses least.

## Goal, next 90 days

Double monthly revenue to 8k. The realistic route is the existing audience buying the bundle rather than a single product, plus consistent content driving new traffic, not a paid campaign she cannot yet afford.

## Channels

- **Active:** Instagram, 2,100 followers, posts once or twice a week, no consistency. Already converted to a Business account and linked to a Facebook Page.
- **Dormant:** TikTok account created, three videos, nothing since March.
- **Owned:** Email list of 610 from website signups. Emailed twice ever.

The email list is the most underused asset in the business.

**Destinations.** Website lumenskin.co.uk with product pages and a bundle page, which is where most revenue sits. Link in bio currently points at the homepage rather than the bundle. No booking link, this is ecommerce. Sender name on email is Priya, replies come to hello@lumenskin.co.uk.

**Baselines, today.** Instagram 2,100 followers. TikTok 180 followers, dormant. Email list 610, emailed twice ever. 340 customers, 31 per cent reordered. Roughly 4k GBP a month.

## Source material

Topics only, not voice. What Priya's customers are already reading and asking each other.

- r/SkincareAddiction and r/Rosacea, for the questions asked repeatedly and the products people say ruined their skin.
- Three dermatologist accounts on Instagram and TikTok that her customers already trust, watched for which ingredients are being discussed that week.
- Two ingredient-science creators who explain formulation without selling anything.
- The National Eczema Society and British Association of Dermatologists, for the flare-up and trigger guidance her audience half remembers.
- Two competing sensitive-skin brands, watched for their claims and their launch timing. Topics only. Never voice.
- A fragrance-free and low-irritant product newsletter her customers subscribe to.
- Her own inbox and DMs, which are the best source she has and the one she reads least systematically.

## Voice

Warm but unsentimental. Talks about skin the way someone talks about a condition they actually have, not the way a brand talks about a category. Specific about ingredients without lecturing. Comfortable saying a product will not work for someone.

Reads as a person, not a brand. First person singular throughout, "I" not "we". Short paragraphs, frequent line breaks. Uses questions to open, then answers them plainly. No exclamation marks. No emoji beyond the occasional single one at the end.

Verbatim phrases: "your skin isn't broken, it's overwhelmed", "I wasted about four hundred quid finding this out", "less is genuinely more here, I'm not being coy", "if you're flaring, stop everything".

## Flags

- Instagram already Business account and linked. No blocker.
- Email list of 610 completely unused. Biggest immediate opportunity and the content engine should feed it.
- Personal story is the strongest proof and she avoids using it. Push on this in the voice work.
- No paid budget. Everything must be organic.
- Only 2,100 followers, so the inbound machine matters more than reach in the first 90 days.
